thread.title: Apple: Teens Say They Want iPhones and Watches - Barron's

title: Apple: Teens Say They Want iPhones and Watches - Barron's
text:
Photo: Tiernan Ray for Barron By April 10, 2018 11:44 a.m. ET 
Teen consumers, it appears, dig Apple . 
A Tuesday report from PiperJaffray, which analyzed a survey of 6,000 U.S. teenagers, included a number of findings relevant to technology companies and consumer brands. For Barron’s Next 50 stock Apple (AAPL), the findings seem particularly timely. 
The company, generally expected to refresh its iPhone lineup this year , stands to benefit considerably if the survey’s finding—that 84% of teens say their next phone purchase will be an iPhone—comes true. (Both that number, and the 82% who said they currently own one, were highs when compared with past surveys. ) Illustration: PiperJaffray 
Getting more people into the Apple network early can be extremely valuable, especially if they also sign up for services that make them unlikely to switch to other phones. And the finding that interest in the Apple Watch is also growing would only help that. (Apple took over the market share lead in smartwatches last year.) Illustration: PiperJaffray 
Most teens don’t plan to purchase watches in the next six months, according to the survey, but the percentage who do plan to buy a smartwatch in the next 6 months—26%—was well ahead of the survey’s historical average of 17%.
